messages:
olivia: Customer on our hosted API reports consistent JSON parse errors when consuming SSE/streaming in JSON mode. They say the payload is valid if downloaded fully, but streaming clients see truncated final token (missing trailing '}' or closing array bracket).
chris: Which client and proxy stack are they using?
olivia: iOS app behind corporate reverse proxy -> traffic path: app -> corp-proxy -> our edge (CloudFront) -> nginx ingress -> backend. They see 'Unexpected end of JSON input' in their client logs.
priya: Do we have the raw TCP/edge logs or an example request id?
olivia: Customer provided curl session and our request-id: req_0a7b2c. Attached curl to reproduce: ```curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?mode=json"``` They say last SSE event sometimes arrives as empty or connection ends before last chunk.
john: I wonder if any intermediate is coalescing/truncating chunk boundaries. Nginx proxy_buffering can buffer and then close upstream connection with keepalive without flushing final small chunk.
chris: Can you paste the small snippet of what the truncated stream looks like?
olivia: From their client capture: `..."choices":[{"text":"hello","finish_reason":"stop"}]` then stream ends (missing final `}` and final newline/event). Client parsing fails.
priya: Repro steps I ran from my laptop behind a simple nginx reverse proxy: 1) start a small nginx with default proxy_buffering on 2) run curl -N against our stream 3) occasionally curl ends with stream missing final `}\n` 4) toggling proxy_buffering off fixed it.
chris: That matches a known class of bugs where proxy merges chunked responses and waits for buffer fill or timeout to flush. If the client closes early or TCP FIN races, the last bytes might be in the upstream buffer and never make it to the client.
olivia: Customer uses corporate proxy which likely has similar buffering. They can't change it. They want a server-side mitigation.
john: On our side: are we sending final SSE event in its own chunk? We do normally flush after final event, but compression/HTTP/transfer layer might re-chunk.
priya: Quick debugging commands I used: ```# reproduce raw streaming with netcat to observe chunks
curl -v -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?mode=json" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'``` Also captured via tcpdump to confirm final packet isn't in client capture when nginx buffering on.
chris: Potential mitigations: 1) emit an explicit heartbeat/terminator event after final JSON (e.g., `event: end\ndata: \n\n`) so even if braces missing client sees end marker 2) ensure we flush final chunk with a larger boundary or `flush()` call in our runtime 3) provide JSON-safe envelope where each SSE data is its own top-level JSON object (less brittle) 4) recommend proxy config fixes (proxy_buffering off, proxy_tcp_nodelay on).
olivia: Customer tried adding retries and they still parse fail because missing bytes produce malformed JSON, not a recoverable error. They asked for a server-side patch.
john: I'll open a runtime task to add a ``terminator`` SSE event after stream completes, opt-in flag for JSON-mode streaming. That will be a quick stopgap.
chris: Also add a note in docs about intermediate proxies coalescing chunk boundaries and impacting streaming structured output, and include the nginx snippet: ```location / { proxy_pass https://upstream; proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; }```
priya: For longer term, we should instrument how often we see truncated final-token reports. I can add a metric that increments when a stream completes with non-empty last-event but client reports parse error or we detect client disconnect within Xms of final write.
olivia: Ticket created: SUP-4234, linked to runtime task INF-981. I notified customer and asked for their proxy config and packet capture.
support-bot: Created support ticket SUP-4234 and linked INF-981. Assigned to john and priya. :white_check_mark:
ingress-bot: Observability note: edge req req_0a7b2c shows 200->FIN from client 74ms after last write. Backend reported all bytes written.
chris: Action items: john add terminator event (opt-in) + small rollout, priya add metric and doc blurb, support to request proxy config/capture from customer.
olivia: Customer accepted workaround (terminator event patch) temporary. They're going to try corporate proxy vendor change long-term.
john: I'll open PR with implementation and a short test that simulates a proxy that drops final small chunk. Will link here when up.
priya: I'll draft the docs warning and recommended nginx snippet.
olivia: Thanks team, keep me posted. :pray:
